This Practice Note is intended only as a general guide and must be read in 
conjunction with the relevant legislation. It contains The Authority’s

associated practices, procedures and instructions. 

Under Section 12 (2) of the Tax Administration Jamaica Act, 2013 a Practice Note 
is binding on the Commissioner General and all officers of The Authority until it is 
revoked. However, taxpayers are reminded that the publication of a Practice Note 
does not affect their right of objection and appeal or their right of access to the 
Revenue Court on points concerning their own liability to Income Tax. 

Comments and suggestions for the improvement of issued Practice Notes and 
suggestions for future Practice Notes are always welcome.

some date other than December 31st.   

The examples in this Practice Note are strictly for purposes of illustrating the issues and 
concerns identified by Tax Administration Jamaica in making decisions on such approvals. 

All references herein are to the Income Tax Act unless otherwise indicated.

I. Glossary of Terms and Abbreviations 

The following list defines various terms used in this Practice Note. 

Accounting Period 

Basis Period 

An accounting period, in bookkeeping, is the period with reference to which 
accounting books of any entity are prepared. It is the period for which books 
are balanced and the financial statements are prepared. Generally, the 
accounting period consists of 12 months. 

According to the First Schedule of the Income Tax Act, basis period is, “for any 
year of assessment, … subject to sub-paragraph (2), the period on the profits 
or gains of which income tax for that year falls to be finally computed in 
respect of the trade in question”. That is, the accounting period in a particular 
Y/A for which a taxpayer is required to compute taxable profit and tax liability 
for Income Tax purposes. 

Body corporate 

A person, association, or group of persons legally incorporated 

Chargeable Income  

Section 2 of the Income Tax Act - "chargeable income" means the aggregate 
amount of income of any person from all sources remaining after allowing the 
appropriate deductions and exemptions under this Act. 

Default period 

Emoluments 

The default period for tax purposes is the "year of assessment", i.e. the period 
of twelve months commencing on the 1st day of January in each year. 

Includes, in relation to any office or employment of profit, items as defined in 
Section 2 of the ITA.  

First Effective Year 

This is the first year of the newly requested accounting period. It is the first 
taxable year for which a change in annual accounting period is effective.  

Financial Year 

A financial year is a period of twelve months, used by business, and other 
organizations in order to calculate their budgets, profits, and losses. It is any 
annual period at the end of which a firm's accounts are closed and financial 
reports are prepared. Section 2 of the CA stipulates that, in relation to a body 
corporate, this is the period in respect of which any profit and loss account of 
the body corporate, laid before it in general meeting is made up, whether 
that period is a year or not. 

Gains or profits of 
any trade, 
profession or 
business 

Any compensation, payments or benefits due to or received by any person in 
the furtherance of a trade, business or profession. Section 2 of the Income 
Tax Act defines "trade" to include every trade, manufacture, adventure or 
concern in the nature of trade.  The term “Profession has not been defined in 

1

the Act but its literal meaning as defined by many scholars and accountancy 
bodies identifies it as a vocation, or a job requiring some thought, skill and 
special knowledge like that of accountant, lawyer, doctor, engineer, architect 
etc. So profession refers to those activities where the livelihood is earned by 
the persons through their intellectual or manual skill. Section 5 of the Income 
Tax Act of Jamaica gives more meaning to “profits or gains” which are 
chargeable to income tax. 

For the purposes of this PN,  and in keeping with its use and context in 
Section 6 of the ITA, this is a period of time between two events or dates. 

For the purposes of this PN, a modified PN refers to where the substance of a 
previously published PN is being changed. For e.g., if a previous PN held that a 
principle applied to ‘A’ but not to ‘B’, and the new PN holds that it applies to 
both ‘A’ and ‘B’ the previous PN is modified because it corrects a published 
position. 

For the purposes of the Practice Note a “newly registered business” is a 
person who has not previously filed an income tax return for any year of 
assessment and who will be filing the first return using a ending date other 
than the 31st  day of December. 

Permitted accounting period, in relation to any person, means the accounting 
period, other than a 12-month period ending December 31st, in respect of 
which the gains or profits of any trade, profession or business carried on or 
exercised by that person are permitted or required to be computed pursuant 
to Sections 6 (2), 6 (3), 5, or 6 (4) of the ITA.

For the purposes of this PN this describes a situation where the new PN does

Section 2 of The Revenue Administration (Amendment) Act, 2013 defines a 
“taxpayer” to include a person who 
(a) Is liable to pay tax pursuant to a revenue law of Jamaica whether or not –  

(i)  The person is resident of Jamaica; 
(i)  The tax liability is in question; or 
(ii)  In the event, any payment is waived or remitted or no amount is 

found to be payable; 

(b) Is of relevance to a treaty partner in respect of an international tax 

agreement. 

Tax Year  

The year for which an income tax return is being filed.  It is usually a particular 
period of twelve months beginning on January 1st and ending on December 
31st. 

The Authority 

means Tax Administration Jamaica as established by section 4  of the Tax 
Administration Jamaica Act, 2013; 

Transitional period 

Transitional Return  

Year of Assessment  

This is the period after the end of one permitted accounting period/ default 
year of assessment and the end of another permitted accounting period or 
default year of assessment. It “bridges” the gap between the previous end 
date and the proposed new end date. This period will always begin from the 
first day of the month following the year end date of the pervious accounting 
period which was in use and the end date of the new accounting period. This 
period may not necessarily cover a 12 month period for filing purposes. 

The changeover from one terminal date to another (whether from the default 
period to a PAP or from one PAP to another or PAP to the default period) 
requires a return to be lodged for the transitional period. The transitional 
period will more likely be for a period of other than 12 months. 

Section 2 of the ITA defines this to mean “the period of twelve months 
commencing on the first day of January in each year”. For persons using a 
permitted accounting period it is implicitly expected that the period of twelve 
months will be retained ending on the date so approved.

III. Purpose of the Practice Note 

1.  The  purpose  of  this  document  is  to  provide  guidance  to  the  public  in  general  on  the 
interpretation of the provisions of Sections 6 (2), 6(3), & 6(4) of the Income Tax Act of 
Jamaica and more specifically, guidance on the application and approval for a permitted 
accounting period, i.e. an accounting date terminating on a date other than 31st day of 
December.  

2.  This PN sets out the factors to be taken into consideration when making a request to the 
CG to allow an alternative accounting period, other than one ending December 31st. 

3.  This  PN  seeks  to  ensure  that  the  decision  on  whether  to  allow  an  entity  to  adopt  a 
permitted accounting period involves balancing the interests of that entity with that of 

4

the Revenue thereby ensuring an efficiently administered income tax system.  

IV. Objectives  

The objectives of this Practice Note is to: 

4.  To provide guidance to persons affected by the law and to the officers of TAJ.  This is in 
accordance  with  Section  12 of  the  Tax  Administration  Jamaica  Act,  2013  which  states 
that the CG may issue Practice Notes setting out the interpretation and procedures for 
the application of the Law; 

5.  Promote and achieve consistency in the administration of the Laws relating to domestic 
tax. It is also to be used to streamline the processing of applications for approval of a 
permitted accounting period to improve efficiency and service to taxpayers; 

6.  Provide taxpayers with certainty regarding specific policies, guidelines and administrative 
procedures concerning the application and approval for a change of accounting year end 
to some date other than 31st day of December, i.e. a permitted accounting period; 

7.  Provide  taxpayers  with  certainty  regarding  specific  policies,  guidelines  and  procedures 

where approval was granted by the CG: 

(a)  For a change in accounting year to some date other than  31st day of December 

and the taxpayer makes a subsequent request for another change.  

(b) For a change in accounting year to some date other than  31st day of December 
and the taxpayer has now made a subsequent request to revert to the default year 
ending 31st day of December; and  

8.  Provide taxpayers with certainty regarding specific policies, guidelines and procedures 

where no approval was granted by the CG: 

(a)  For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December. 

(b) For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December 
and the taxpayer has now made a subsequent request to revert to the default 
year ending 31st day of December.

V. Scope & Background  

9.  In administering the law relating to a permitted accounting period, this Practice Note sets 
out the interpretation and administrative rules of the CG in respect to Section 6 of the ITA 
governing  the  change  in  accounting  period  to  a  permitted  accounting  period.  It  also 
provides TAJ’s position with respect to the submission of an application for approval of 
the change.  

10. The requirement for the approval of any planned change in an entity’s accounting period 
for income tax purposes has long been in existence and must be done in accordance with 
the law. However, there were no recommended rules and guidelines for instructing the 
taxpayer on how to secure this approval for a permitted accounting period. 

11. Where a date other than the default period is being used and the CG is not aware of this, 
the taxpayer’s income tax account on TAJ’s database will not reflect this change. As such, 
the CG intends to ensure that the Revenue Administration Information System is properly 
configured to evaluate the expectations of each taxpayer who is required to file returns.  

12. Therefore,  if  an  existing  taxpayer  wishes  to  change  their  accounting  period  from  the 
default  period  to  any  other  12-month  period  or  a  new  taxpayer  wishes  to  adopt  an 
accounting period other than the default period, the net income shall, with the approval 
of the CG, be computed on the basis of such new proposed accounting period. 

13. In considering a request to change to a permitted accounting period, the CG will look at 
relevant matters, consistent with the statutory responsibilities under Section 6 of the ITA 
so as to maintain the integrity of the tax system. 

14. A permitted accounting period affects the deadlines/due dates for paying income tax and 

filing of an Income Tax Return. 

VI. Need for a policy guideline 

15. There was no fixed period within which to make the request to secure the approval of the 
CG. The ITA is silent on a required timeframe within which to make a request for securing 
the CG’s approval for a permitted accounting period. 

16. There was no clear instruction provided where a permitted accounting period is used and 
there  is  an  underpinning  expectation  that  the  filing  of  income  in  respect  of  a  year  of 

6 

 
                                                                                               
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 01-2022                                                                                         

assessment must cover a period of 12 months.  

17. For taxpayers who have been using a permitted accounting period and request to revert 
to the default January to December filing period there are challenges which exist which 
may see a year of assessment with more than 12 months.  

18. There was no clear instruction advising the taxpayer how to separate the income when a 
new business files its first account of the trade and the income must be apportioned at 
even rate between twelve months and the remaining months in the reporting period. 

19. Section 6 did not expressly prescribe that the relevant income for a new business that is 
filing its first set of accounts may be accounted for on two separate returns. The section 
did not make provisions for a late penalty charges that would now be applicable under 
Section 71B and interest charges under Section 79 (2a). At the time Section 6 was written 
into law a late filing penalty provision was not yet brought into law. 

20. Stakeholders are uncertain about the filing obligation in respect of their first return and 
its impact on their request for a PAP; when the date of incorporation does not coincide 
with the commencement date of trading. 

21. Section 6 (2) of the ITA establishes that a person can make a request for permission for 
their accounting year to end on a date other than the 31st day of December.  However, 
there is no provision for instances where an individual has multiple sources of income, 
inclusive of emoluments. 

VII. Statutory requirements for a permitted accounting period 

22.  Sections 6(2), 6(3) & 6(4) of the ITA generally provides that a taxpayer who wishes to 
change  its  accounting  period  and  use  a  permitted  accounting  period  must  obtain  the 
approval of the CG. (See Extracts) 

23.  Section 6 (2) provides that, in conjunction with subsection (1), where the CG is satisfied 
that any person usually makes up the accounts of his trade, profession or business to 
some date other than the 31st day of December he may permit the gains or profits of 
that trade, profession or business to be computed upon the income for the period of 
twelve months terminating on that date in the year of assessment to which the accounts 
of that trade, profession or business are usually made up.  

24.  Section 6 (3) of the ITA provides that where a person commencing to carry on a trade, 
profession or business satisfies the CG that he/she intends to make up the accounts to a 

7

date other than the 31st day of December, the CG may grant permission under subsection 
(2). 

25.  Where permission is granted as per Section 6 (2) and under circumstances where 

(a)  the first accounts of the trade, profession or business have not yet been drawn 

up; and  

(b) the first accounts of a trade, profession or business covers a period which exceeds 

twelve months,  

the income of the period shall be treated for this purpose as being apportioned at an even 
rate between the twelve months terminating on the date to which the accounts are made 
up and the remainder of the period.   

26. Under  Section  6  (4)  of  the  ITA  where  a  person  departs  from  his  permitted  accounting 

terminal date, i.e.  his ending date.  

(a)  The new permitted accounting period will be determined by the CG identifying:  

(i)  The Y/A in which the departure occurs and 
(ii)  The Y/A immediately following the departure period 

(b) The permitted accounting period determined by the CG for the Y/A in which the 

departure occurred may include any interval between 

(i) 
(ii) 

the end of the old accounting period and 
the commencement date of the new permitted accounting period. 

(c)  The terminal date of the new permitted accounting period as determined by the 
CG will be regarded as the permitted accounting terminal date of this person until 
another permitted accounting period has been requested in accordance with the 
provisions of the legislation and the guidelines of this PN.  

27. After a determination of the taxpayer’s permitted accounting period has been made by 
the CG in accordance with section 6 (4), if the taxpayer subsequently chooses to change 
his permitted accounting period, the taxpayer must first seek approval from the CG. Any 
further applications for change will be assessed in accordance with the criteria set out in 
section 6(2) & (3) of the Income Tax Act.

IX. Taxpayers’ Obligations 

32.  The taxpayer must submit a request for the use of a permitted accounting period using 
the  eservices  account.  Step-by-step  instructions  can  be  found  on  TAJ’s  website 
https://www.jamaicatax.gov.jm/web/guest/how-to..  “How-to  Request  Permitted 
Accounting Period Approval via eservices” (Exhibit 1) 

33. For income tax purposes, any taxpayer who proposes to change his accounting year end 
shall, before using  the  new period,  comply  with the provisions  of  the  ITA  relating to  a 
permitted accounting period by securing the approval of the CG to change the accounting 
year end to some date other than the 31st day of December.  

34. For a newly registered business (NRB) the CG, in using his discretionary powers, will allow 
new registrants to identify and adopt the period so specified as its permitted accounting 
period when they file their first set of accounts of the trade. This permission will allow 
them  to  file  their  first  accounts  of  the  trade  with  a  year-end  other  than  31st  day  of 
December on or before the due date for the relevant year of assessment (year in which 
the accounting year ends).  

35. A NRB, filing of its first set of accounts, and intends to use a date other than December 
31st,  will  not  be  required  to  complete  an  application  (PAP01).  Instead  the  NRB  will  be 
permitted by the CG to proceed in filing its first return using the date so identified, this 
filing will now become its de facto application, thereby granting permission to use such.  

36. The  NRB  must  be  aware  that  where  it  is  required  to  file  an  income  tax  return  under 
Section 71A that this provision is adhered to. However, the NRB, in filing its first return as 
is  required  under  Section  71A  of  the  ITA,  may  have  challenges  in  fully  complying  with 
subsequent provisions within. (See Section XX). 

37.  Further to paragraph 34, where upon commencement of trading, the first set of accounts 
of a NRB (who has been allowed to identify and adopt a PAP) exceeds twelve months 

10 

 
                                                                                               
 
 
  
 
 UPN-PAP 01-2022                                                                                         

they  will  be  required  to  apportion  their  income  at  an  even  rate  between  the  twelve 
months ending on the terminal date of the accounts and the remainder of the period.  

38. In the ITA it is implicitly interpreted that one return is to be filed for the twelve-month 
period and another return for the remainder of the period. Legislation has given the CG 
the powers to instruct the taxpayer on how to file the two separate returns. Both returns 
must be aligned to the permitted accounting period being requested.  The CG has further 
instructed that:  

the  1st  return  should  cover  the  apportioned  income  representing  the 
shorter period (See Section XIX- Transitional Return) and 
the  2nd  return  will  cover  the  apportioned  income  representing  the 
remaining 12 months.  

The relevant credits and capital allowances should be applied in each Y/A.  

X. Who will be allowed a permitted accounting period? 

39. Section 6(2) of the ITA provides for any person to request an approval for a permitted 

accounting period. 

40. Section 2 of the ITA defines “person” as any individual and also as any body of persons. 
"Body  of  persons"  means  any  body  politic,  corporate  or  collegiate,  and  any  company, 
fraternity, fellowship and society of persons, whether corporate or not corporate. 

41. Bodies  corporate,  regardless  of  business  type  may  be  permitted  to  change  their 
accounting period to end on some date other than December 31st. Generally, individuals 
must adopt the calendar year as their default period; however, Section 6 of the ITA does 
not preclude them from requesting a change.  

42. While partnerships are not 'persons' for tax purposes, there is nothing to prevent the CG 
from allowing such entities to adopt a PAP where they can demonstrate circumstances 
which makes it acceptable to make such a request. The net income of a partnership or a 
partnership loss is not attributable to a partner until the end of the partnership income

XIX. Transitional period & Transitional return  

72. Section 2 of the Act defines “year of assessment” to mean “the period of twelve months 
commencing  on  the  first  day  of  January  in  each  year.  Where  a  permitted  accounting 
period is used there is an underpinning expectation that the filing of income in respect of 
a year of assessment must cover a period of 12 months.  

73. There is a distinction which is to be made between a transitional period and a year of 
assessment. The transitional period is the practical mechanism which is applied in order 
to facilitate the operation of the permitted accounting period (which is to constitute a 
year of assessment). Where an entity is allowed to adopt a PAP there is a change to the 
end date of its accounting period, which results in a transitional period of more or less 
than 12 months. Therefore, a transitional period is not a “year of assessment” as defined 
by the Act and therefore the 12-month limit should not to apply.  

74. The transitional period is the period after the end of one permitted accounting period/ 
year of assessment and the end of another permitted accounting period or default year 
of assessment. This period will always begin from the first day of the month following the 
year end date of the pervious accounting period which was in use and the end date of the 
new accounting period. 

75. The CG recognizes that in practical terms a transitional period of less than 3 months would 
be  administratively  inconvenient.  However,  there  are  instances  when  this  cannot  be 
avoided.  Nonetheless,  in  order  to  give  practical  application  to  the  operation  of  the 
statutory provisions of the permitted accounting period, the CG may, in the exercise of 
his  discretion,  make  administrative  decisions  so  as  to  give  practical  effect  to  those 
statutory provisions, so as to ensure that the law and the systems are in accord. In such 
instances,  the  CG  has  instructed  that  he  will  accept  a  transitional  return  with  a  basis 
period outside the 12-month criteria.

from a previously approved permitted accounting period and return to the default filing
